title: Vicious
text: “Ah… I was wondering what on earth could’ve gotten me called out in the middle of the night, and it turns out it was that whole business with Itsuki going on a rampage.”
“……There was that, yes.”

Rabbit Guy sighed as he recalled it, I say. What had happened, apparently, was that a little while back Itsuki had brought Riska and Rabbit Guy along, had them wait near some noble’s mansion, and snuck in alone to scout it out—only to discover a party underway where demi-humans and beastmen were being abused. Not the sort of party where they’d merely been getting high on some sketchy drugs, mind you—drugs were involved, but it was an utterly nauseating affair on top of that. Apparently a bunch of people, all worked up on drugs, had been laughing while they tortured and abused slaves in some kind of cruel spectacle, grinning the whole while. Even if Itsuki hadn’t become Riska, even if he hadn’t been tortured into abandoning justice, the sight he’d witnessed there was apparently horrific enough that anyone might have given up on justice and turned to evil after seeing it.

“It was such a ghastly affair that it made me think humanity itself has no business existing in this world. Before I knew it, I found myself thinking I should capture every last one of them and make them suffer the same fate.”

Itsuki had knocked out every single person at that party single-handedly, using paralysis and sleep spells, before calling Father to have them transported away. Overnight, countless people vanished from that mansion, turning it into a local ghost story about a “man-eating manor,” and as the presumed culprit, Itsuki’s bounty within Melromarc shot up dramatically.
“What kind of mind thinks to make a bath out of the blood of tortured demi-humans and soak in it, I wonder…”
“It was undeniably a horrific scene, but still…”

And so, on Itsuki’s orders, every last one of those captured had been shipped off to Siltvelt. After enslaving them, Father, myself, Itsuki, and Ren—who’d been hastily summoned for the occasion—used the Portal Skill to send them flying off to Siltvelt, so it was over in the blink of an eye.
“Trees, monsters, demi-humans, beastmen—I’m fine with all of them. But humans ought to go extinct eventually. Don’t you think, at this rate?”

“How do I put this… you’re starting to look like some ex-detective about to fling open the gates of some demon realm… I might genuinely need to send you off for treatment. I just pray it doesn’t come to the point where Itsuki turns into a demon lord and we have to do something about it.”
“I haven’t fallen that far. There are people like Rishia-san out there, after all. If we don’t dispose of the rot, everything ends—that’s the whole reason I was summoned here.”
“Hmm……”
Itsuki really was extreme, I say.
“I’d hate to think a party like that’s happening over in Siltvelt too, but honestly, when it comes to sheer cruelty, they might not lose to anyone… rot doesn’t discriminate by place.”

For a moment, the eyes with which Itsuki gazed upon his despair toward humanity overlapped, in my mind, with the eyes Ark used to watch the reincarnators without a trace of anger. Of course, compared to that, even Itsuki’s eyes were mere child’s play—Ark’s gaze had been the truly chilling kind. Father, back in the first world, had worn a similar look at times, as if resigning himself to something. Thinking that Ark, too, must have carried something that weighed on him just as heavily, my chest ached. Whether I myself carried as much light within me as that man hoped for… I couldn’t say.
“Anyway, don’t go thinking either side is entirely in the right, okay? There are extremists on the demi-human side too.”
“I know that. We can’t keep chatting forever, can we? Please, go on ahead.”
“Yeah.”
“Well then, off we go, I say.”

Naturally, I wasn’t about to ride in a carriage pulled by Rival’s parent, I say. I rode alongside on Yuki-chan instead, I say. Oh? Father from the first world seemed startled by Yuki-chan’s sudden appearance. Hadn’t I kept quiet about her until now, he wondered? In truth, she’d been appearing in the show ever since the trapeze act at the circus, I say. Naturally, Kou had been taking part too, I say. Yuki-chan was a Filolial-sama with a bit of tolerance for the slave trade, I say. The reason being, as a thoroughbred, she understood the logic of training relative to one’s own price, I say.
“I do hope you find some good slaves, Motoyasu-sama.”
“Indeed I do. Father, is there anything to report?”

“Hmm… according to Sadeena and the others, most of the survivors have already been secured, so it’s shifted mostly to trading now. I’ve asked Shion if there’s anyone he recognizes, just in case, though.”

Apparently Big Sister and the others had passed along descriptions of people who might still be out there. Crocodile Guy, accompanying us in his beastman form, rode along silently with his arms crossed. Perhaps concentrating his spirit? He carried the air of a warrior about him. Father turned his gaze toward him.
“Shion… have you given up on humanity, like Itsuki has?”
“……It’s not that I can’t understand the feeling, but I know for a fact that there are good people too. Even at today’s circus, there were some who looked displeased at the abuse.”
“Yeah. That’s true. The ones who get excited over the extreme stuff stand out, but there are good people too. By the second half, everyone was enjoying themselves, weren’t they?”
“Indeed.”

“Anyway, Shion, you’ve really bulked up in a short time, haven’t you? You’ve gotten so muscular… your reaction to the whipping in the first act got noticeably weaker, so we were talking about maybe pulling you from that bit?”
“T-that is… if at all possible, I would like to continue performing in it…”
Apparently, perhaps because it was the very first act he’d done, Crocodile Guy still wanted to stay in it.
“There is a plan to cast a weakening spell on you before the whipping, but… you’re just too muscular, Shion. The way you’d wince in pain would end up looking unnatural.”
“……What a troublesome thing. To seek strength and have it lead to an unwanted result.”
Crocodile Guy let out a heavy sigh.
“Well, maybe because Shion’s physique in beastman form has such good aesthetic appeal, some fans have started showing up for you? Doesn’t seem to matter what race they are, either.”
“I don’t know how to react to that. I’d like whoever feels goodwill toward me despite having no real interest in me to consider my position for once.”
“I quite agree, I say.”

Even now, from time to time, some pig hands me a letter, I say. Apparently they’ve started arriving occasionally since I began performing at the circus, I say. Since I can’t understand pig-speak even when summoned, I turn them down, I say. Ah, though per Father’s orders, I’m not allowed to hurl insults—so I decline politely, I say. I go to meet them carrying Yuki-chan and Kou on my shoulders, I say.

“For one reason or another—faces and all sorts of things draw attention, you know—Shion, Motoyasu-kun, Wolf, Teo, they all give off this intelligent vibe, and there’s actually been a fair number of nobles wanting to buy them lately. Probably why Teo’s been walking around in beastman form these days.”
Just like with Big Sister, every slave Father purchases somehow ends up rated more highly in looks!
“If anything, I’m more worried about what sort of crowd is interested in me… what exactly are they seeing when they look at me?”
Father smiled at Crocodile Guy’s question.
“About sixty percent are women. They keep saying things like how muscular you are and how beautiful your scales look.”
“……Isn’t it my hide they’re actually after?”

Father turned his face away just slightly. I happen to know there were pig parents out there hunting for crocodile-leather bags, I say. I suppose the same sort of story holds true in this world as well, I say.
“Isn’t this really the fault of a certain Shield Hero who polishes his own scales and hide every chance he gets?”

Father would, from time to time, use his free moments to polish Crocodile Guy’s scales, treating it as an extension of massage therapy. Crocodile Guy, for his part, enjoyed it too, relaxing into it and ending up with even shinier scales as a result. Éclair had even teased him about becoming quite the handsome fellow.

“No, no, it’s just—the more you polish it, the shinier it gets, and that’s just satisfying, you know? It’s the same with Teo’s and Wolf’s fur, isn’t it? Even if half of them are after the hide, isn’t the other half captivated by Shion’s physique?”
“Gyaaah!”
Oh? Rival’s parent let out a cry at just the right moment while pulling the carriage.
“Come to think of it, dragon hide was supposedly popular material too… I wonder if nobles like to show off luxury bags and wallets made from it.”
“I rather think a dragon would make more suitable material than myself.”
Seemed to be a shared worry among the reptilian sort, I say.
